PROTAC-DB 4.0: an expanded knowledgebase of targeted protein degradation modalities with AI-powered knowledge discovery.

ProtoPure: Literature Mining and Analysis of Protein Purification Protocols at Proteome Scale.

ProtoPure is a literature-mining resource that systematically extracts and organizes protein purification protocols from the published literature at proteome scale, addressing the current reliance on ad hoc, case-by-case literature reviews. It aggregates purification conditions and strategies across many proteins, enabling researchers to identify effective procedures based on biochemical similarity rather than manual searching of a dozen papers.

Domain-Aware Enzyme Classification via Multiple Instance Learning.

This paper introduces a multiple instance learning approach for predicting Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers that focuses on functional domains rather than whole-protein embeddings. By treating domains as instances, the method preserves local catalytic signals that whole-sequence embeddings tend to dilute, while avoiding the need for accurate 3D structures required by structure-based alternatives. The approach aims to improve protein function annotation and metabolic pathway reconstruction.

Microbiome science needs AI competence, not just AI literacy.

The authors argue that microbiome researchers need deeper AI competence—not just basic literacy—because common pitfalls like data leakage, incomplete metadata, ecological confounding, and unverified generative-AI outputs can yield convincing but biologically misleading conclusions. Species phylogenetics using intraprotein residue dependence inferred with protein foundation models.

This preprint proposes using protein foundation models (pFMs) to infer phylogenetic relationships from patterns of dependence between residues within proteins, rather than relying on traditional alignment-based substitution models that assume site independence. The authors compare two pFM types—ESM models for individual sequences and MSA Transformer models for alignments—and extract residue and sequence attention matrices as phylogenetic signals. The approach aims to capture intraprotein residue dependence that conventional methods ignore.

De novo Design of a Vanadium Haloperoxidase.

This preprint reports the de novo design of a vanadium-dependent haloperoxidase, an enzyme that catalyzes carbon-halogen bond formation. The key challenge was that the vanadate cofactor is an anionic oxometalate requiring a precise hydrogen-bonding and electrostatic network rather than the coordinate-covalent bonds used for typical metal cofactors. The work demonstrates that computational protein design can be extended to this unusual cofactor-binding mode, opening a route to engineered halogenases.

LongVerse: verified AI agents for Nanopore and PacBio DNA methylation analysis.

LongVerse is an AI-agent system that converts a single English sentence into haplotype-resolved DNA methylation calls from Nanopore or PacBio reads, with agents that configure a pinned pipeline rather than writing code. On the HG002 reference genome, agent and human expert outputs were byte-identical (r = 1.000) and agreed well with bisulfite sequencing (r = 0.943 and 0.884), at a cost of $0.12–$0.54 per run. The work demonstrates verification of agent outputs against an independent measurement rather than rubric or LLM-judge scoring.
